chunks: Electron vs hole mobility. The question: Which charge carriers are more mobile: holes or electrons?
Mobility tells you how quickly a carrier moves when pushed by an electric field.
In silicon, electrons are more mobile than holes: about 1350 versus 480 in the same units, a ratio of roughly 2. 8. That one fact has big practical effects.
N-type devices are faster and conduct better than P-type devices of the same size.
Picture two runners crossing a field. The electron runs a smooth, simple track.
The hole has to move by a more crowded route, where neighbors keep passing the gap along, and it ends up slower. Same push, different path, so a different speed.
The analogy is only a picture: a hole is really an empty spot, and its "heaviness" comes from the way the silicon's energy bands are shaped.
Electrons have one conduction-band curve of moderate curvature.
Holes occupy the valence band, where the heavy-hole and light-hole branches meet at the top (degenerate at k equals 0 ).

The flat heavy-hole curve corresponds to a large effective mass; holes populate it heavily because it has a larger density of states, and they scatter readily between branches and into the nearby split-off band.
The parabolic picture is only a rough sketch; real silicon has six anisotropic conduction valleys and warped valence bands.
Mobility ( micro ): how fast a carrier drifts per unit of field. Effective mass: how heavy a carrier acts when pushed. Heavier means slower.
Majority carrier: the plentiful carrier type. NMOS and PMOS: transistors whose current is carried by electrons or by holes.
Drive current: how much current a transistor can supply when on.
Say an NMOS transistor whose conducting channel is drawn 1 µm wide gives some amount of current. A PMOS of the same width carries holes, so it gives only about 1/2. 8 as much.
To match the NMOS, you make the PMOS about 2. 8 times wider, so roughly 2. 8 µm. In practice designers use about two to three times. That is the whole idea.
"Electrons are more mobile: about 1350 versus 480 cm²/V·s in silicon, a ratio of roughly 2. 8. Mobility is q tau over m^ .
Electrons have a lighter conductivity effective mass and a simpler band to move in, while holes sit in the valence band with heavy and light hole bands and more scattering.
That's why PMOS devices are drawn wider than NMOS, NPN transistors beat PNP, and N-type material has lower resistance at the same doping."
